title: The first superconducting final focus quadrupole prototype of the FCC-ee study

predicted_errors.error_location: Section describing quench protection: 'Multiple taps within the joint box... A 50 Ω crowbar connected to a 75 Ω dump resistor is employed for energy extraction.'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: A 75 Ω dump resistor carrying the stated magnet current of 765–1000 A would develop 57–75 kV across it. Such a high voltage is not realistic for a small prototype superconducting magnet quench-protection/dump circuit; typical dump resistors are on the order of milliohms to limit extraction voltage. The stated '50 Ω crowbar' is also inconsistent with a crowbar function, which is normally a low-impedance bypass. This strongly suggests a unit error (Ω vs mΩ) or a fundamentally misdescribed protection circuit.

predicted_errors.error_location: Field-quality discussion: 'We have not repeated the extra step done at warm which reduced multipole errors and consisted of rotating the magnet by about 45° with respect to the measuring system...'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Rotating the magnet by 45° relative to the measuring system is a measurement-calibration/correction technique used to separate or cancel probe/systematic harmonics; it does not physically reduce the magnet's own multipole errors. The text says this step 'reduced multipole errors' without clarifying that it reduces measured/probe-related errors, which misleadingly attributes a change in the magnet's field quality to the measurement procedure.
